introduction_markdown: Multiple choice paper (0510 Biology 1, June 2024, Ordinary Level, General Certificate of Education Board). Duration: one and a half hours. Answer ALL 50 questions; all questions carry equal marks. Each question has four suggested answers A, B, C and D; select only one answer for each question. Non-programmable calculators are allowed.
enonce_intro_markdown: **Multiple choice questions** - choose the one correct answer, A, B, C or D. Section I (questions 1-7): independent questions. Section II (questions 8-20): biological diagrams. Section III (questions 21-25): one or more responses correct. Section IV (questions 26-30): pairs of statements. Section V (questions 31-40): lettered headings and a description. Section VI (questions 41-50): biological situations.

figures.legende: Drawing of a yeast cell with a chain of smaller cells growing out of it (Question 8).
Circular life cycle: Housefly, Egg, X (stage to identify), Pupa, back to Housefly (Question 9).
Larynx, trachea, bronchi and lungs with labels 1 to 4; label 3 points to a bronchus, 4 to the fine bronchioles (Question 10).
Alimentary canal of man with labels L, M, N and O (Question 11). The scan is faint and a line of text shows through the page.
Mould fungus (Mucor type) with hyphae and two sporangia, labels 1 to 4 (Question 16).
Cross section of a hibiscus flower with labels Anther, Stigma, Style, Petal, Sepal and Stalk (Question 19).
Bacterial cell with a flagellum and layers, labels 1 to 4 (Question 20).
Graph of rate of enzyme reaction against temperature (20, 37, 50 and 60 degrees C): bell-shaped curve with the optimum at 37 degrees C (Question 43).

incertitudes: Questions 26, 27, 30, 38 et 48 : clé discutable (énoncés de type assertion-raison dont le lien causal est interprétable, ou deux options exactes), donc passées en questions OUVERTES ; la clé la plus probable est indiquée dans le corrigé (26 A, 27 B, 30 B, 38 C, 48 C).
Question 21 : clé B (eau et sels minéraux) ; un correcteur strict pourrait ne retenir que l'eau (D), mais la transpiration entraîne bien les sels minéraux dans le flux xylémien.
Question 31 : aucune articulation ne tourne réellement de 360 degrés et l'articulation en pivot n'est pas proposée ; clé B (articulation en rotule, la plus proche).
Question 11 : le scan est pâle et le texte de la page voisine transparaît ; seule l'option A est cohérente avec L = oesophage et M = estomac (N et O désignent le foie et la vésicule biliaire).
Question 16 : clé B lue sur le schéma (le repère 4 désigne la paroi arrondie du sporange) ; le schéma est de faible qualité.
Question 10 : le repère 3 touche le tube annelé qui entre dans le poumon (bronche) ; schéma de faible contraste.

Fautes d'impression conservées : Q4 « Is a pain receptor », Q7 « gaseous exchange », Q13 phrase interrogative sans verbe, Q21 et Q34 et Q38 « Carbondioxide » et « Sulphurdioxide », Q25 « form a region », Q43 « graph below show » et « catalyzed », Q46 « colour indicate », Q41 option A sans point final.

Q21 à Q25 (une ou plusieurs réponses correctes) et Q26 à Q30 (assertion-raison) : les options A à D sont les combinaisons imprimées en tête de section, recopiées comme choix ; les consignes de chaque section sont résumées au début de la première question de la section.
Les filigranes et publicités de la page (gcerevision.com) ont été ignorés.

questions.enonce_markdown:
*SECTION I - directions as printed, summarised:* Each of these questions or incomplete statements is followed by four suggested answers. Select the best answer in each case.

Which of the following organisms has all the following parts: vacuole, cell membrane, chloroplast and pyrenoids?
questions.corrige_markdown: Spirogyra is a filamentous green alga: each cell has a vacuole, a cell membrane, a spiral chloroplast and pyrenoids (starch-storing bodies) in the chloroplast. Bacteria have no chloroplast or true vacuole, Amoeba is an animal-like protozoan without chloroplasts, and yeast is a fungus (no chloroplast, no pyrenoids). **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: If a lake is polluted by untreated sewage, it would turn to have:
questions.corrige_markdown: Sewage is rich in nitrates and phosphates, so algae multiply quickly (eutrophication, an algal bloom). When the algae die, bacteria decompose them and use up the dissolved oxygen, so the oxygen content falls and fish die. Options B, C and D are the opposite of what happens. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which structure assists the amoeba both in food capture and movement?
questions.corrige_markdown: The amoeba moves by pushing out pseudopodia (false feet) of cytoplasm, and it also uses them to surround and engulf food particles. The food vacuole only digests the food, the plasma membrane is a boundary, and the contractile vacuole removes excess water (osmoregulation). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Is a pain receptor on the skin of man:
questions.corrige_markdown: Pain is detected by free nerve endings in the epidermis. Pacinian corpuscles detect deep pressure, Meissner's corpuscles detect light touch, and the hair plexus detects the movement of hairs. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Where does implantation take place in the female reproductive system?
questions.corrige_markdown: After fertilization in the oviduct (the Fallopian tube) the zygote divides and the embryo travels to the uterus, where it embeds in the thick, blood-rich uterine lining. This embedding is implantation. The oviduct and the Fallopian tube are the same organ (C and D) and the cervix is the neck of the uterus. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The left side of the heart is thicker than the right side because it pumps blood:
questions.corrige_markdown: The left ventricle pumps blood to the whole body (the systemic circulation), which is far from the heart, so it needs a thick muscular wall to produce a high pressure. The right ventricle pumps blood only to the nearby lungs. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: During gaseous exchange in humans, oxygen is sent into the lungs as a result of:
questions.corrige_markdown: During inspiration the intercostal muscles contract (ribs move up and out) and the diaphragm flattens. The volume of the thorax increases, so the pressure inside falls below atmospheric pressure and air (with oxygen) rushes into the lungs. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Increase in thoracic pressure and decrease in thoracic volume.
Decrease in thoracic volume and decrease in thoracic pressure.
Increase in thoracic volume and decrease in thoracic pressure.
Decrease in thoracic pressure and no change in volume.

questions.enonce_markdown:
*SECTION II - directions as printed, summarised:* This group of questions relates to biological diagrams. Select the best answer for each question.

The mode of reproduction in the yeast above is

![fig-1](gce-ol-biology-2024-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_1.png)
questions.corrige_markdown: The diagram shows a large yeast cell with smaller cells growing out of it in a chain. A small outgrowth (bud) forms on the parent cell, receives a copy of the nucleus and finally breaks off. This is budding, a type of asexual reproduction. Conjugation occurs in Spirogyra, fragmentation in filamentous organisms, and sporulation needs spores. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The stage "X" on the life cycle below represents:

![fig-2](gce-ol-biology-2024-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_2.png)
questions.corrige_markdown: The housefly has complete metamorphosis: egg, larva (maggot), pupa, adult. In the cycle, Housefly leads to Egg, then to X, then to Pupa, so X is the larva. Imago and adult are the same stage as the housefly itself, and a nymph belongs to incomplete metamorphosis (e.g. grasshopper, cockroach), where there is no pupa. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The diagram below is a cross section of part of the respiratory system in man.

![fig-3](gce-ol-biology-2024-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_3.png)

The structure labelled 3 represents:
questions.corrige_markdown: In the diagram, 1 is the larynx at the top, 2 is the trachea (ringed tube), 3 is one of the two branches of the trachea going into a lung (a bronchus) and 4 is the fine branching tubes inside the lung (bronchioles). **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The diagram below is that of the alimentary canal of man.

![fig-4](gce-ol-biology-2024-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_4.png)

Identify the parts labeled L M N O.
questions.corrige_markdown: L is the long tube at the top, the oesophagus (gullet), which carries food to the stomach. M points to the large muscular bag on the right, the stomach. N and O point to the organs beside the stomach, the liver (large, on the left) and the gall bladder (small sac under the liver). Only option A starts with L = oesophagus and M = stomach; every other option misplaces L or M. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: L Oesophagus, M Stomach, N Liver, O Gall bladder
L Oesophagus, M Gall bladder, N Stomach, O Liver
L Stomach, M Liver, N Gall bladder, O Oesophagus
L Liver, M Gall bladder, N Oesophagus, O Stomach

questions.enonce_markdown: The part of the leaf with numerous chloroplast is:
questions.corrige_markdown: The palisade layer is made of tall, tightly packed cells just under the upper epidermis, and it contains the most chloroplasts, so most photosynthesis happens there. The spongy mesophyll has fewer chloroplasts, and the epidermis (except the guard cells of the stomata) has none. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The part of the mammalian eye that refracts light first during image formation?
questions.corrige_markdown: Light enters the eye through the transparent cornea, which bends it most strongly (large change of speed from air to cornea) before it passes through the aqueous humour, lens and vitreous humour. The pupil is only an opening in the iris and does not refract light. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Where does meiosis occur in the male reproduction system?
questions.corrige_markdown: Sperm cells are formed by meiosis in the seminiferous tubules of the testes. The epididymis only stores and matures sperms, the scrotum is the sac that holds the testes, and the penis delivers semen. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A structure which carries water from the roots to the leaves:
questions.corrige_markdown: Xylem vessels are long, hollow, lignified tubes that carry water and mineral salts upwards from the roots to the leaves. Phloem carries manufactured food (sucrose) in both directions, the cuticle is a waxy waterproof layer and the epidermis is a protective layer. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Below is the structure of a mould fungus:

![fig-5](gce-ol-biology-2024-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_5.png)

The structure numbered 4 functions in:
questions.corrige_markdown: The diagram shows a mould such as Mucor or bread mould. Label 1 is the hyphae that absorb food and secrete enzymes (rhizoids), 2 is the upright sporangiophore, 3 is the mass of spores, and 4 is the round outer wall of the sporangium, which encloses the spores until it bursts and releases them. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which part of the mammalian brain is responsible for voluntary activities of the body?
questions.corrige_markdown: The cerebrum (cerebral hemispheres) controls conscious thought, memory and voluntary movements. The hypothalamus controls temperature and water balance, the cerebellum controls balance and coordination, and the medulla oblongata controls involuntary actions such as breathing and heartbeat. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The sensory neuron plays a role in conducting impulses from the:
questions.corrige_markdown: A sensory (afferent) neuron carries impulses from a receptor (sense organ) to the central nervous system (brain or spinal cord). Option B and C describe the wrong direction, and in D the impulse does not go directly to the motor neuron (it passes through the central nervous system, via a relay neuron in a reflex arc). **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Receptor to the central nervous system.
Central nervous system to the sensory organ.
Effector to the central nervous system.
Sensory receptor to the motor neuron.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The diagram below is a cross-section of a hibiscus flower

![fig-6](gce-ol-biology-2024-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_6.png)

Which part is responsible to attract insects for pollination?
questions.corrige_markdown: In an insect-pollinated flower the petals are large and brightly coloured (and often scented) to attract insects. The stigma receives pollen, the anther produces pollen, and the sepals protect the flower bud. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Below is a diagram of a bacterial cell.

![fig-7](gce-ol-biology-2024-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_7.png)

Which structure is labelled 1?
questions.corrige_markdown: Label 1 points to the long, thin, whip-like thread that comes out of the cell: it is the flagellum, used for movement. Labels 2, 3 and 4 point to the outer layers of the cell and to the genetic material inside. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
*SECTION III - directions as printed, summarised:* For each of the questions below, ONE or MORE of the responses is (are) correct. Decide which of the responses is (are) correct. Then choose: A if 1, 2 and 3 are all correct; B if 1 and 2 only are correct; C if 2 and 3 only are correct; D if 1 only is correct.

Transpiration helps plants to take up:

1. Water.
2. Mineral salts.
3. Carbondioxide.
questions.corrige_markdown: Transpiration (evaporation of water from the leaves) creates the transpiration pull, which draws water up the xylem and, with it, the dissolved mineral salts, so water (1) and mineral salts (2) are taken up and carried to the leaves. Carbon dioxide (3) enters the leaves by diffusion through the open stomata; it is not taken up because of transpiration. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
In rats black fur colour is dominant over white fur colour. A cross between a homozygous black male and a homozygous white female produces offspring which are all:

1. Black.
2. White.
3. Black and white.
questions.corrige_markdown: Let B = black (dominant) and b = white. Homozygous black is BB and homozygous white is bb. The cross BB x bb gives only Bb offspring (F1), and since black is dominant, all of them are black. White (2) and a mixture (3) do not occur. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Reptiles:

1. Are poikilothermic.
2. Have moist scaly skin.
3. Are all terrestrial.
questions.corrige_markdown: 1 is true: reptiles are cold-blooded (poikilothermic), so their body temperature changes with the surroundings. 2 is false: their scaly skin is dry, not moist (moist skin belongs to amphibians). 3 is false: some reptiles live in water (crocodiles, turtles, sea snakes). Only 1 is correct. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
When there is overheating in the body:

1. More blood flows to the skin surface.
2. Less blood flows to the skin surface.
3. There is an increase in metabolic rate.
questions.corrige_markdown: When the body is too hot, the arterioles of the skin dilate (vasodilation), so more blood flows near the skin surface and more heat is lost (1 is correct, 2 is wrong). The metabolic rate does not increase: it decreases or stays constant, since a higher rate would produce more heat (3 is wrong). **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
During active transport:

1. Molecules move from a region of high concentration to a region of low concentration.
2. Molecules move form a region of lower concentration to a region of high concentration.
3. Energy is required.
questions.corrige_markdown: Active transport moves substances against the concentration gradient, from low to high concentration (2 is correct), using energy from respiration (ATP) (3 is correct). Movement from high to low concentration (1) is diffusion, which is passive and needs no energy. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
*SECTION IV - directions as printed, summarised:* Each question consists of a statement in the left-hand column followed by a second statement in the right-hand column. Choose: A if both are true and the 2nd statement is a correct explanation of the first; B if both are true and the 2nd statement is NOT a correct explanation of the first; C if the first is true and the second false; D if the first is false and the second true.

**First statement:** Photosynthesis occurs only during the day.

**Second statement:** Chlorophyll absorbs solar energy in sun light.

*Options as printed:* A) True, True: the 2nd statement is a correct explanation of the first.   B) True, True: the 2nd statement is NOT a correct explanation of the first.   C) True, False.   D) False, True.
questions.corrige_markdown: Both statements are scientifically true as general facts: chlorophyll absorbs light energy (mainly red and blue light) and uses it to make glucose from carbon dioxide and water. The difficulty is the word "only" in the first statement: in nature photosynthesis does need sunlight, so it happens during the day, but it can also take place at night under artificial light, so a strict reading makes the first statement false (answer C). If the first statement is read as "in natural conditions", the second statement explains why light is needed (answer A). Because two keys are defensible, this question is left open for self-assessment. Most likely intended key: **A** (both true, and the second explains why photosynthesis needs daylight).

questions.enonce_markdown:
**First statement:** Yeast cells carry out fermentation.

**Second statement:** Ethanol is a product of anaerobic respiration in breweries.

*Options as printed:* A) True, True: the 2nd statement is a correct explanation of the first.   B) True, True: the 2nd statement is NOT a correct explanation of the first.   C) True, False.   D) False, True.
questions.corrige_markdown: Both statements are true: yeast ferments sugar to ethanol and carbon dioxide in the absence of oxygen (glucose $\rightarrow$ ethanol + carbon dioxide + energy), and this is how beer is made in breweries. Whether the second statement is a "correct explanation" of the first is a matter of interpretation: it describes a product and an application of fermentation, but it does not explain why yeast cells ferment (strictly answer B), although the paper may intend it as supporting evidence (answer A). Because two keys are defensible, the question is left open. Most likely intended key: **B** (both true, second is not an explanation).

questions.enonce_markdown:
**First statement:** Nitrogen fixing bacteria converts soil nutrients to atmospheric nitrogen.

**Second statement:** Nitrogen fixation is either done aerobically or anaerobically.
questions.corrige_markdown: The first statement is false: nitrogen-fixing bacteria do the opposite, converting atmospheric nitrogen gas into ammonia or nitrogen compounds (nitrates) that plants can use. Changing soil nitrates back into nitrogen gas is done by denitrifying bacteria. The second statement is true: Azotobacter fixes nitrogen aerobically and Clostridium anaerobically. So the first is false and the second is true. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: True, True: the 2nd statement is a correct explanation of the first.
True, True: the 2nd statement is NOT a correct explanation of the first.

questions.enonce_markdown:
**First statement:** During very cold weather, the erector pili muscles contract and cause hair on the body to stand erect.

**Second statement:** During cold weather there is increase in metabolic activities which causes more blood supply to the skin surface.
questions.corrige_markdown: The first statement is true: in the cold the erector pili muscles contract, the hairs stand up and trap a layer of air that insulates the body. The second statement is false: although the metabolic rate may rise (shivering), the blood supply to the skin surface is reduced, not increased, because the arterioles of the skin constrict (vasoconstriction) to cut down heat loss. So the first is true and the second is false. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: True, True: the 2nd statement is a correct explanation of the first.
True, True: the 2nd statement is NOT a correct explanation of the first.

questions.enonce_markdown:
**First statement:** Plants are autotrophic.

**Second statement:** Plants always occupy the first trophic level in an ecosystem.

*Options as printed:* A) True, True: the 2nd statement is a correct explanation of the first.   B) True, True: the 2nd statement is NOT a correct explanation of the first.   C) True, False.   D) False, True.
questions.corrige_markdown: Both statements are true: plants make their own food by photosynthesis (autotrophic), and as producers they are always the first trophic level of a food chain. The link between them is a matter of interpretation: being autotrophic is the reason why plants are producers, so the first statement explains the second rather than the other way round (strictly answer B), but the paper may intend the second as a correct explanation (answer A). Because two keys are defensible, the question is left open. Most likely intended key: **B** (both true, second is not an explanation of the first).

questions.enonce_markdown:
*SECTION V - directions as printed, summarised:* Each question consists of four lettered headings A, B, C, D. Select the heading which is closely related to the description which follows.

Select the heading which is closely related to the description: an example of a joint that can rotate 360°.
questions.corrige_markdown: A ball and socket joint (shoulder, hip) allows movement in all directions and rotation, so it is the joint that comes closest to rotating through 360°. A hinge joint moves in one plane only (like a door), a fixed joint does not move, and a slightly moveable joint (between vertebrae) allows only a little movement. Note: strictly, no joint turns through a full 360°, and a pivot joint is not offered, so B is the best answer. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Select the heading which is closely related to the description: a feeding relationship between two organisms in which one benefits but the other neither benefits nor loses.
questions.corrige_markdown: In commensalism one organism benefits while the other is neither helped nor harmed. In parasitism the host loses, in mutualism both benefit, and symbiosis is the general word for a close living together (including mutualism). **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Select the heading which is closely related to the description: provides turgidity to plant cells.
questions.corrige_markdown: A turgid cell is fully swollen with water. The strong cellulose cell wall resists the pressure of the swollen vacuole and keeps the cell firm and in shape, so it provides turgidity (support) to plant cells. The cell membrane only controls what enters and leaves, the chloroplast makes food and the nucleus controls the cell. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Select the heading which is closely related to the description: a water pollutant.
questions.corrige_markdown: Fertilizers (nitrates and phosphates) are washed from farmland into rivers and lakes and pollute the water (eutrophication). Carbon dioxide, smog and sulphur dioxide are air pollutants. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Select the heading which is closely related to the description: a primary consumer.
questions.corrige_markdown: A primary consumer is the first consumer in a food chain: it eats producers (plants), so it is a herbivore. Carnivores and omnivores that eat other animals are secondary or higher consumers. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Select the heading which is closely related to the description: a condition in which alleles blend to produce an intermediate trait.
questions.corrige_markdown: In incomplete dominance neither allele is fully dominant, so the heterozygote shows a blend (e.g. red x white snapdragon gives pink). In complete dominance the dominant allele hides the other, and phenotype and genotype are only the appearance and the genetic make-up. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Select the heading which is closely related to the description: separates the right auricle from the right ventricle.
questions.corrige_markdown: The tricuspid valve (three flaps) lies between the right atrium (auricle) and the right ventricle and prevents backflow. The bicuspid valve is on the left side, semilunar valves are at the exits of the ventricles, and the septum separates the left and right sides of the heart. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Select the heading which is closely related to the description: a product of fermentation in plants.

*Options as printed:* A) Carbondioxide.   B) Water.   C) Ethanol.   D) Lactic acid.
questions.corrige_markdown: In plants (and yeast) the fermentation of glucose is alcoholic: glucose $\rightarrow$ ethanol + carbon dioxide + a little energy. The usual textbook contrast is ethanol in plants and lactic acid in animals, so the intended key is probably C (ethanol). However carbon dioxide (A) is also a product of fermentation in plants, so two options are correct and the question is left open for self-assessment. Water (B) is not a product of fermentation, and lactic acid (D) is the product in animal muscle. Most likely intended key: **C**.

questions.enonce_markdown: Select the heading which is closely related to the description: detects vibrations in water.
questions.corrige_markdown: The lateral line is a row of sense cells along the sides of a fish that detects vibrations and pressure changes in the water. Scales protect the body, gills exchange gases and the tail fin propels the fish. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Select the heading which is closely related to the description: an adaptation of birds to flight.
questions.corrige_markdown: Birds have a streamlined body shape that reduces air resistance in flight. Their body temperature is high (not low), they have large, strong flight muscles (not small and flat), and a sharp beak is related to feeding, not to flight. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
*SECTION VI - directions as printed, summarised:* This group of questions deals with biological situations. Each situation is followed by a set of questions. Select the best answer for each question.

The bending of a plant shoot towards unidirectional light source is the result of:
questions.corrige_markdown: Auxin is made at the shoot tip. With light from one side, auxin moves to the shaded (darker) side, where it makes the cells elongate faster than on the lighted side, so the shoot bends towards the light (positive phototropism). Auxin accumulating on the lighted side (A) would make the shoot bend away from the light. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Accumulation of auxins on the lighted side
A decrease in the amount of water in the cells of plant.
Accumulations of auxins on the darker side.
An increase in the rate of water loss from the leaves.

questions.enonce_markdown: If a cell has 16 chromosomes, how many chromosomes will each of its daughter cells have after mitosis.
questions.corrige_markdown: Mitosis produces two daughter cells that are genetically identical to the parent cell, so the chromosome number stays the same: 16. Halving to 8 happens in meiosis. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The graph below show the effect of temperature on an enzyme catalyzed reaction.

![fig-8](gce-ol-biology-2024-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_8.png)

What will cause a fall in the curve at temperatures above 40°C.
questions.corrige_markdown: The rate rises up to the optimum temperature (37 °C on the graph), then falls steeply above about 40 °C because the high temperature destroys the shape of the enzyme's active site: the enzyme is denatured, and it cannot be restored. Enzymes are not used up in a reaction, and they are not activated by a rise in temperature beyond the optimum. Deactivated is the weaker word used for low temperatures, where enzymes are only inactive and not destroyed. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What is the use of pyrogallic acid in the experiment to demonstrate the importance of oxygen during seed germination?
questions.corrige_markdown: Alkaline pyrogallol (pyrogallic acid) absorbs oxygen. It is placed in the tube of the control-experiment set-up so that the seeds are in an atmosphere without oxygen, and they fail to germinate in comparison with seeds in air. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: To cause the seeds to germinate.
To provide more water for the seeds.

questions.enonce_markdown: A seedling transplanted on a hot windy day withers because the:
questions.corrige_markdown: On a hot, windy day the rate of transpiration is high. The roots of a newly transplanted seedling are damaged and cannot replace the water lost, so the seedling loses more water than it takes in, its cells lose turgor and it wilts. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A solution from crushed germinating maize seeds was heated with an equal amount of Benedict's solution in a test tube and a brick red colour appeared. The brick red colour indicate the presence of:
questions.corrige_markdown: Benedict's solution, heated with a reducing sugar, turns from blue to green, yellow, orange and finally brick red. Starch is tested with iodine solution (blue-black), lipid with the ethanol emulsion test, and protein with the biuret test (violet). The sugar here (maltose) comes from the digestion of starch during germination. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A food chain differs from a food web in that:
questions.corrige_markdown: A food chain is one straight line of feeding, each organism eating one kind of food. A food web is many interconnected food chains, so an organism in a web has more than one food source. Option C is the reverse, option D describes a web, and the loss of energy at each stage is the same in both. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Each organism in a food web has more than one food source.
Little energy is lost in a food web
Each organism in a food chain has more than one food source.

questions.enonce_markdown:
In an experiment to test for the presence of starch in a green leaf, the leaf is boiled in water, then in alcohol. Why must the leaf be boiled in water?

*Options as printed:* A) To burst starch grains.   B) To remove chlorophyll.   C) To destroy the protoplasm.   D) To make it soft.
questions.corrige_markdown: Boiling in water kills the leaf cells: the protoplasm and cell membranes are destroyed, enzymes are denatured so that no further change in starch occurs, and the leaf becomes soft and permeable so that iodine can enter. Chlorophyll is removed by the hot alcohol, not by the water (B is wrong), and starch grains are not burst (A is wrong). Both C (destroy the protoplasm) and D (make it soft) are accepted textbook reasons, so two options are defensible and the question is left open for self-assessment. Most likely intended key: **C**.

questions.enonce_markdown: In a farm land, it is noticed that maize plants found amongst leguminous plants, were seen to grow more vigorously than in areas where the leguminous plants were absent. How can this be explained?
questions.corrige_markdown: Leguminous plants have root nodules containing nitrogen-fixing bacteria (Rhizobium), which convert atmospheric nitrogen into nitrogen compounds (nitrates). These enrich the soil with nitrogen, which the maize uses to make proteins and grow vigorously. The other options do not explain better growth. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: The leguminous plants make more water available to the maize plants.
The leguminous plants provide shade to the maize plants.
The leguminous plants increase the nitrogen content of the soil.
The leguminous plants conserve more soil water.

questions.enonce_markdown: The planting of more trees in an environment will cause:
questions.corrige_markdown: Trees photosynthesize, taking in carbon dioxide and releasing oxygen, so planting more trees gives more oxygen (and less carbon dioxide). Tree roots bind the soil and the canopy reduces the impact of rain, so soil erosion and leaching decrease. **Answer: C.**
